title: שמעון בן עזאי
author: Heilprin source tradition; Warsaw digital witness
attribution: Fresh project English, authored from the frozen Hebrew and revised through source-informed author and independent model review. Editorial-layer attribution in the Warsaw witness remains qualified.

paragraphs: 1. Avot, chapter 4; Berakhot 9:4; Yoma 2:3; Ta'anit 4:4; Shekalim 3:1, 4:6, 5:3; Yevamot 4:13; Sotah 3:4, 9:15; Bava Batra 9:10; Horayot 1:2; Zevahim 1:3; Bekhorot 9:5; Kinnim 2:5, 3:6; Niddah 5:8; Parah 1:1, 3; Yadayim 3:5, 4:2.

2. In Yevamot 63, end of side b, he said that anyone who does not engage in procreation is as though he sheds blood and diminishes the divine image. They said to him, “You expound well, but do not fulfill well.” He answered, “What shall I do, when my soul longs for Torah? The world can be maintained through others.” Tosafot write: although Af al Pi implies that he married R' Akiva's daughter, for it says there, “R' Akiva's daughter did the same for Ben Azzai,” we say in the first chapter of Sotah that he married her and divorced her; see there, 4b, and Midrash Mishlei, at “She rises while it is still night.” In Jerusalem Sotah, chapter 1, halakhah 2: “What is the duration of intercourse? Ben Azzai says ….” It asks: but Ben Azzai never married a woman in his life! Some say that he became sexually aroused; others say that he had intercourse and separated; others say, “The Lord's secret is for those who fear Him.”

3. A pupil-colleague of R' Akiva: Shekalim, chapter 3, and Bava Batra 158b. Rashbam explains that initially he was his pupil and finally his colleague. Sefer Keritut and the author of Etz Hayyim write that this is implied in Pesahim 18; I did not find it there. In Jerusalem Rosh Hashanah, first chapter, end of halakhah 1: Ben Azzai was R' Akiva's colleague and pupil, and so forth; some say, pupil and colleague. They disagree whether he was initially a colleague and R' Akiva became wiser, or initially his pupil and Ben Azzai became wiser. See Beit Yosef, Yoreh De'ah, no. 10 as cited (compare no. 242), and what I wrote in my work on Ketubbot 69a, “Huna our colleague.” He said, “All Israel's sages are like a garlic peel, except for this bald one”—R' Akiva; see R' Yehoshua ben Korhah. He said, “I am not answering R' Akiva's words, but adding”: beginning of Sifra. In Rabbah, end of Naso: R' Akiva said …; Ben Azzai said, “I am not answering my teacher's words, but adding.” Heilprin attributes to R' Yonatan, “Alas for you, Ben Azzai, that you did not attend R' Akiva.” In Nedarim 74b, Ben Azzai says this of himself. He asked R' Yonatan, “What does Yishmael say about this?” Ben Azzai said of himself, “Alas for Ben Azzai, who did not attend R' Yishmael”: Hullin 70b and Rashi there. There, 71a. He followed R' Akiva into the privy and learned three things. R' Yehudah said to him, “Were you so bold toward your teacher?” He answered, “It is Torah, and I need to learn”: Berakhot 62a; see above, R' Akiva. He spoke before R' Akiva in R' Yehoshua's name: Mishnah Yoma 2:3, 25a. In Mishnah Ta'anit 4:4, R' Akiva returned to reciting as Ben Azzai did. Nahum of Gam Zu whispered to R' Akiva that nine kav suffice for one who has had a seminal emission; Ben Azzai expounded it publicly, see his entry. Because Ben Azzai did not marry, saying that the world could be maintained through others, he therefore expounded it publicly because of the neglect of procreation: Berit Shalom, Aharei Mot. Ben Azzai is placed before his teacher R' Akiva; see the reason in Tosafot, Sotah 4a, and in the rules in the introduction, according to the order of occurrence.

4. In Hagigah 14b, he entered the Pardes and died young. Of him it says, “Precious in the eyes of the Lord is the death of His faithful ones.” This accords with what is said in Berakhot 57b: whoever sees Ben Azzai in a dream should expect piety. Berit Shalom, Aharei Mot. In Yalkut Tehillim, chapter 9, “He has not forgotten the cry of the humble”: He does not forget the blood of the righteous killed in the days of persecution, such as R' Akiva and his colleagues, Ben Azzai and R' Yehudah the baker. I did not find that he was killed; it was mentioned above that he died.

5. He was one of the five who argued before the sages; see Danin. In every matter of wisdom the Talmud mentions him: Abaye said, “I am like Ben Azzai in the marketplaces of Tiberias,” and Rava used the same words. Rav and R' Yohanan used a similar expression; see his entry. Rashi, Ba-Kol Me'arevin, explains that in their days there was no one who uprooted mountains as he did; see what I wrote there under Abaye. Ben Azzai made the Mekhilta from “These are the names” to the end of the Torah: Yuhasin, בסדה״ד [provisionally, in the order-of-generations section], at the end of the discussion of the priests; see above, R' Hoshaya. When he died, the diligent ceased (end of Eglah Arufah). The cited Mishnah reads השקדנים, “the diligent”; the Warsaw transcription here reads השקרנים, “the liars.”

6. And R' Elazar ben Mattyah and Hananyah ben Hakhinai. R' Yohanan ben Yeshua agreed with Ben Azzai. Heilprin calls him Akiva's father-in-law here; Mishnah Yadayim 3:5 calls him the son of Akiva's father-in-law. R' Yohanan reports in his name; see his entry. R' Yonatan: see above. R' Yose ben Dormaskit.
